1) Integration scope: embeddings + reranker for top-K candidate scoring; structured output for downstream enrichment (tool calling later).

3) Immediate blocker you mentioned on the call: intermittent 5xx errors when invoking the embed->reranker flow (appears around peak ingestion).

Thanks Marissa — attaching a small log extract and the minimal request that reproduces the 5xx.

What we see: when a batch of ~50 documents arrives, our pipeline calls the Redwood embeddings endpoint, then the reranker endpoint. About 1 in ~200 requests to the reranker returns a 5xx (502 / 503), typically during peak ingestion (09:30–10:15 PT). The payload attached (finlytics-logs-20260816.txt) shows two sample requests and the server response headers.

Example request (we're using your JS SDK, v0.9.2):

const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, timeout: 60000 });

const res = await client.reranker.rank({
  model: 'redwood/reranker-v1',
  input: candidates,
  query: queryText,
  top_k: 5
});

We do set timeout=60000ms. We also use a short-lived API key rotated hourly via our internal vault.

Let us know what additional headers you need.

—Caroline
CTO, FinLytics
caroline@finlytics.com

Hi Caroline — thanks for the logs and the SDK snippet. I've started a local repro using your payload. A few quick checks while we dig in:

- Can you confirm whether you use our streaming API for the reranker or non-streaming (single response)? The SDK call you sent looks non-streaming.
- Please also paste the exact Authorization header value pattern (you can redact the token body, e.g., Authorization: Bearer xxxxx.xxxxx). We need to confirm there's no middleware rewriting the header at your edge.

Temporary mitigations to try immediately: 
- Increase client-side retries on 5xx (exponential backoff) and add a jitter.
- Try reducing batch size from 50 -> 16 to see if it's strictly correlated to request size.
- If you aren't already, enable connection pooling in the Node SDK (agent keepAlive) to avoid TCP churn.

I'll attach a small patch to the SDK client config that turns on keepAlive and a retry wrapper. If you're able to apply it, please run the same ingestion for an hour and send back the logs.

Snippet to run as a quick cURL sanity check (non-SDK):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/rerank
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"redwood/reranker-v1","query":"test","input":[{"id":"1","text":"sample"}]}'

I'll keep iterating — tagging Neha for deeper model-side checks.

Thanks,
Camila

Subject: Re: Next steps — FinLytics integration & repro plan

Thanks for the reproducer and logs. I ran the payload through our staging reranker and observed two noteworthy things: 

1) Sporadic 5xxs line up with a specific request shape where the candidate list includes a few very large documents (text length > 25k chars). The model path currently has an OOM-protection fast-fail that returns 502 when memory pressure spikes. We should either truncate client-side or switch to streaming/segmented ranking.

2) Your current request shows top_k: 5 and no explicit kv_cache hints. If you are re-ranking many similar queries in short succession, enabling our prefix KV cache will reduce token re-encoding and lower memory/latency spikes.

Immediate recommendations (order matters):
- Client: add a pre-send sanitizer that clips documents above 10k chars, return an action flag so you can rerun long docs in a separate flow.
- Client: enable keepAlive + retry wrapper (Camila's patch).
- Server: we can bump the per-request memory cap for your dedicated routing policy while we monitor. I'll propose a temp increase for 48–72 hours.

Repro steps for your engineers (what I ran):
- Use the attached finlytics-logs-20260816.txt payload.
- Run the provided cURL above with the same Authorization token your service uses (rotate token if necessary).
- If you see 502s, capture full request+response headers and a heap snapshot (we'll provide a script).

I've attached a short script we use to sandbox the reranker; I also opened SUP-4521 and linked it to this thread so Support can track. I'll coordinate the temp memory cap change once Marissa confirms.

-Neha
